chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Isḥāq al-ʿAlawī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Daylamī, from Furayt, from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said:

I was with Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام when a man from the dealers in khazz entered upon him and said to him: “May I be made your ransom, what do you say about salat (prayer) in khazz?” He said: “There is no problem with praying in it.”

The man said to him: “May I be made your ransom, it is carrion, and it is my trade, and I know it.” So Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said to him: “I know it better than you.” The man said to him: “It is my trade, and no one knows it better than I do.” Then Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام smiled and said to him: “You say that it is a creature brought out from the water, or caught from the water and then brought out, and when water is lost to it, it dies?” The man said: “You have spoken the truth, may I be made your ransom; that is how it is.”

Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “So you say that it is a creature that walks on four, yet it is not within the category of fish such that its slaughter would be its coming out from the water.” The man said: “Yes, by Allah, that is what I say.” So Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said to him: “Then indeed Allah, the Exalted, has made it halal (permissible) and has made its slaughter its death, just as He made fish halal (permissible) and made their slaughter their death.”

key_terms.أَحَلَّهُ: He made it halal (permissible), indicating divine legal permissibility
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship whose validity in khazz is being asked about
key_terms.الْحِيتَانِ: fish, cited as the comparable category in legal ruling
key_terms.الْخَزِّ: khazz, the material or fabric under discussion for use in salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, indicating that the creature comes from and dies without water
key_terms.دَابَّةٌ: a creature or animal, used in describing the nature of the animal in question
key_terms.ذَكَاتُهُ: its slaughter/purification for lawful use, here defined by its death
key_terms.مَيِّتٌ: dead/carrion, referring to the man’s objection regarding the source animal

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in clothing made from khazz according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal discussion with Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام about the permissibility of praying in garments made from khazz. The Imam explains that the animal from which it comes is halal (permissible), and that its valid slaughter is its death, analogous in ruling to aquatic creatures. The narration is significant for jurisprudential rulings on dress in salat (prayer) and the lawfulness of certain animal products.
